name: ATLAS location.list to location

source.name: location.list.txt
source.note: RFC 7946 FeatureCollection emitted by ATLAS. The mapper picks up features[] automatically; each feature is flattened to dotted fields, and geometry is pulled whole with the raw op.

rules.note: Fixed by the type schema. Feature 4 (Texas) is really a gazetteer place, not a location - see the notes below.
ATLAS carries no stable identifier, so ids are minted here. Re-running produces new ids; use source_record_id to deduplicate.
category values must match ^[a-z0-9]+([._-][a-z0-9]+)*$, so ATLAS's Custom / Hazard are lowercased and given clearer names.
ATLAS stores one address blob. The structured fields stay empty until the addresses are re-geocoded.
GeoJSON coordinates are already [lon, lat] in WGS84, which is exactly what geo.point wants - no reordering.
ATLAS records how a point was placed nowhere, and source is 'manual' for every feature, so precision cannot be asserted.
Polygon features become a single boundary shape. Point features skip this rule and use geo.point instead.
Weak natural key - ATLAS has no ids and three features share the name European Wax Center, so these collide. Replace with a real key before treating re-imports as idempotent.

dropped.type: The GeoJSON literal "Feature"; carries no record-level meaning.
dropped.properties.source: Always the string 'manual' in this file; captured once as source_system instead.

followUp: Feature 4 is Texas stored as a bare Point. It is a gazetteer place, not a location - move it to a place record with a real boundary and drop it from this import.
The three European Wax Center features are separate sites of one brand. After import, create an organization record and link each location to it with relations[rel=operated_by].
geo.address.formatted is a single blob. Re-geocode to populate street_address / address_locality / address_region / postal_code / country_code, and to set geo.precision honestly.
geo.place_closure is left empty. Run the containment resolver once the gazetteer exists.
